segments.line: The man on the golden boat is the king's magician.
His name is Djedi. In
the old stories, he could put a goose's head back on after it was cut off. He
takes you up the river to the king.
Khufu himself sits on the throne. You
fly the drone between the columns of his hall. The
guards drop their spears. The
king doesn't flinch. He laughs.
Then he wants to fly it himself. He
pushes both sticks at once. The drone
shoots straight at a column. Your
heart stops. Its
sensors catch it half a metre away, and it just hangs there, humming."
An eye that flies. With this I could see
every corner of Egypt. Every mine. Every enemy." Then he says
the sentence you were afraid of." It belongs to the king."
Djedi leans in and whispers something. You don't speak the language, but
Nefer does. Later, very quietly, she tells you what he said." A
man who commands a sky spirit is more dangerous than an army." The king gives you
an order. At
sunrise tomorrow, you will show him all of Egypt from the sky.
If the eye sees everything, you live. If it doesn't, the magician was right about you. Nefer
squeezes your hand. Nobody says no to a king of Egypt. Not if they want to keep breathing. Back at
the camp, you unfold the solar panel to charge for tomorrow. One of Djedi's men
walks straight across it.
Crack. The
panel still works. Barely. About a tenth of the power.
Now you have one full battery, one at half, and no more sun.
